statutes.act: Read With Section 34 And 324 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: The case of the prosecution against the two accused is that at 8:40 on the night of June 28, 1990, in village Bassi Umar Khan, near the courtyard of Atma Singh, two accused viz, Prem Singh and Deepinder Singh inflicted injuries on deceased Ravinder Singh, son of Mohan Singh.

The motive of the crime is stated to be a pending civil litigation between father of the deceased in the capacity of holder of Power of Attorney on behalf of one Joginder Singh Mahant on one side and Sampuran Singh, father of accused No.1, Prem Singh on the other, regarding the possession of a piece of land in village Bassi Umar Khan.
The alleged offence of murder of deceased is alleged to have been committed on June 28, 1990 at about 8:40 p.m. when the deceased was returning from his field to his house.
After preparing inquest memo., the investigating officer inspected the spot and seized blood-stained earth from near the courtyard of Atma Singh.
Autopsy on the dead body of the deceased was conducted by Dr. Avinash Sood at Civil Hospital, Hoshiarpur at 12 noon on June 29, 1990.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
petitioner_arguments: Atma Singh does not live in the village.
The compound of his house is open.
I was sitting on a cot in his compound.
Ravinder Singh armed with takua, Amarjit Singh, son of Sardara Singh, armed with a dang, came there and attacked me and caused injuries, I raised alarm.
Neighbours came, and inflicted injuries to Ravinder Singh in order to rescue me from Ravinder Singh.
respondent_arguments: The case of the prosecution is highly improbable that-deceased alone was attacked, and Mohan Singh against whom the accused had actual grudge, was allowed to go unhurt.
court_reasoning: The High Court found that civil litigation was against Mohan Singh-PW6 and not against his son deceased Ravinder Singh.
There was a subsequent insertion of entry of dead body of the deceased in the register.
The said tampering with the hospital record indicates that false evidence was created to prove the presence of the two alleged eyewitnesses at the time of the incident
The High Court also found that evidence of recovery of the alleged weapons made on 6th July, 1990 was a fabrication as was also found by the trial court.
holding: The High Court acquitted the accused.
The case is remanded to the trial court for retrial in accordance with law.
